final_answer: CRISPR-Cas9 works by using a guide RNA to locate a specific sequence in the target area. The guide RNA forms a complex with the Cas9 enzyme, which then binds to the target site. Cas9 cuts the two strands of the double helix at a precise position. After the cut, the cell repairs the break. One repair pathway often used is non-homologous end joining, which can lead to small insertions or deletions. Alternatively, if a repair template is provided, the cell can use homology-directed repair to introduce precise changes. This allows for targeted modifications at the chosen location.
